QF.id: AIFM Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_7

question.text: Indus Hybrid AIF is constructing a two-sleeve portfolio: a Private Equity sleeve (weight 60%, σ = 20%) and a Private Credit sleeve (weight 40%, σ = 10%). The correlation between the two sleeves is 0.30. What is the portfolio variance?

explanation.text: The Logic: Two-asset portfolio variance is σp² = w1²σ1² + w2²σ2² + 2·w1·w2·ρ·σ1·σ2. Substituting: (0.6²)(0.20²) + (0.4²)(0.10²) + 2(0.6)(0.4)(0.30)(0.20)(0.10) = 0.01440 + 0.00160 + 0.00144 = 0.01744. The implied standard deviation is approximately 13.2%. The Trap: 0.01600 is what you get if you set ρ=0 (i.e., drop the covariance/correlation term entirely): 0.01440 + 0.00160 = 0.01600. 0.00900 is the squared weighted average of the standard deviations and ignores the variance formula altogether. 0.02000 is a rounded distractor that does not correspond to a clean assumption on these inputs. Note: Always confirm whether you have been given correlation (ρ) or covariance directly; with correlation, you must multiply by both standard deviations to recover the covariance term inside the variance formula.
